dungeons.name: The Keelvaults
dungeons.local_story: A wreck has been built into the harbor vaults. Its failing pumps threaten the shore workers above.
dungeons.wider_story_link: Duplicate harbor copies carry the same false registry trail as the woodland archive, giving the coast a complete alternative story route.
encounter_features: Bilge levels change the available fighting space.
Anchor-chain cover counters a broadside with a visual warning.
A short signal sequence reopens the route to shore; sound always has a visual equivalent.

dungeons.name: The Buried Court
dungeons.local_story: An older water court lies beneath the dunes. Its corrupted judgments still divert water from the living oasis.
dungeons.wider_story_link: The original charter exposes the southern register, providing the desert route’s equivalent final-act evidence.
encounter_features: Redirect shallow water to reveal the real court marks.
Wind and shade create safe movement windows with clear visual cues.
The last verdict is broken through world evidence and a combat mechanic, not a random dialogue guess.

dungeons.name: Rootlock Sluice
dungeons.local_story: Raised homes are flooding because the old sluice is being held shut. Workers need it open, not replaced with another public promise.
dungeons.wider_story_link: Confiscated maintenance plates carry the same collection seal found in the relief records. The warden has been enforcing an altered instruction.
encounter_features: Changing water levels opens short routes with safe retreat points.
A maintenance diagram gives an actual valve solution.
The final boss can be interrupted or countered using a universal release lever.

dungeons.name: Broken Crown Quarry
dungeons.local_story: A lease dispute has become an armed occupation of the quarry. Workers are trapped behind their own equipment.
dungeons.wider_story_link: Wage and lease records reveal the frontier’s branch of the collection network. The local rescue remains meaningful on its own.
encounter_features: Operate a real hoist to open a safe route for rescued workers.
Falling stone has readable ground shadows and safe edges.
The steward’s barriers can be repositioned with winches rather than burned through by one class.
